title: Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan Outstanding Approved Amount and Late Days on an Unpaid Approval
content:
**Rule.** For an approval left unpaid under a Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan, the claim paid is the most recently filed claim on the plan whose handling status is approved. Its outstanding approved amount is the amount of its latest decision less the claim money, net of voids, already paid on it, never below zero; a claim with no decision event on file has nothing outstanding. The late payment is the outstanding approved amount, rounded to the cent.

**Late days.** The late days of the payment are the calendar days from the decision date to the handling date, less the level's payment issue period, never below zero. The payment issue period is 10 days on the $2,000, $3,000, $5,000 and $7,500 Plans and 7 days on the $10,000 and $15,000 Plans.

## Reading the claim's handling history

| Entry | Use |
| --- | --- |
| latest claim decision | its amount and its date |
| claim payments on the claim | subtracted from the decision amount |
| voids of those payments | added back (net of voids) |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A claim's latest decision approved 2,000.00; a payment of 500.00 was issued and later voided in full; no other payment. Net paid is nothing, so the outstanding approved amount is 2,000.00 and the payment is 2,000.00.

On a $5,000 Plan, a decision dated 25 days before the handling date gives 15 late days; on a $10,000 Plan, 18 late days. A decision dated 6 days before the handling date gives none on either.
